THOUGHT: Preoperative vision was 20/20 OU and there is no history of prior sinus surgery, so the intact globe was present immediately before the procedure. Postoperative findings (right periorbital ecchymosis, marked enophthalmos/hematoma) plus CT showing no recognizable globe in the orbit, violation of the lamina papyracea with air tracking into the orbit, and pathological material from the maxillary sinus that contained orbital fat and extraocular muscle indicate that orbital contents were displaced/removed into the sinus. Surgical exploration documented absence of the entire right globe, loss of most orbital fat and muscles, and a severed optic nerve. The combination of an acute perioperative setting, breach of the medial orbital wall, orbital contents found in the sinus specimen, and direct confirmation at exploration is most consistent with an iatrogenic avulsive loss/exenteration of the globe (inadvertent globe removal/avulsion) during endoscopic sinonasal surgery. Alternative possibilities (severe external facial trauma with globe avulsion, rapidly destructive sinonasal malignancy eroding into the orbit, fulminant invasive fungal sinusitis destroying orbital contents, or a planned/previous therapeutic exenteration recorded incorrectly) are far less consistent with the acute preoperative normal vision and the operative/pathologic findings, but are listed below for completeness.

DIAGNOSIS:
1) Iatrogenic orbital exenteration / avulsive globe removal (inadvertent globe avulsion during endoscopic sinus surgery)
2) Acute traumatic globe avulsion from external facial trauma (less likely given no trauma history)
3) Aggressive sinonasal malignancy with orbital invasion causing spontaneous auto-amputation/destruction of the globe and orbital contents
4) Fulminant invasive fungal sinusitis (e.g., mucormycosis) with rapid orbital necrosis and loss of globe
5) Intentional therapeutic orbital exenteration performed previously or misdocumented (iatrogenic but deliberate, unlikely given preoperative vision)
ground_truth: Complete orbital enucleation as a complication of functional endoscopic sinus surgery (FESS)
